meta.title: Forecasting sparse demand: probabilistic SKU forecasts and the cost of getting inventory wrong

audit.note: identical rows present in both yearly sheets
negative lines on non-C invoices are manual adjustments
zero/negative price lines carry no revenue information
first and last calendar weeks are incomplete and excluded

assumptions: Weeks are ISO weeks (Mon-Sun). The first and last calendar weeks are partial and dropped.
Cancellations are returns, not negative demand; they are excluded, never netted.
Demand is units shipped (positive Quantity), not revenue.
Zeros in the spine are observed no-sales; with no stockout data they may hide lost demand.

assumptions.unit_price: median observed price per SKU up to each forecast origin, winsorised at p99.5 (no look-ahead)

price_basis_sensitivity.note: same orders, costed with the pre-origin median price (primary) versus the full-sample median price

assumptions.note: absolute costs scale with the ratio and L; only the comparison is meaningful
